output_json.patch_notes: In AbstractUnArchiver.extractFile, immediately after `final File f = FileUtils.resolveFile( dir, entryName )`, added a guard that compares canonical paths: it computes `dir.getCanonicalPath() + File.separator` and `f.getCanonicalPath()`, and throws `ArchiverException("Entry is outside of the target directory (" + entryName + ")")` unless the resolved file's canonical path starts with the destination directory's canonical path. This is the single shared extraction sink for both the tar path (TarUnArchiver -> extractFile) and the zip path (AbstractZipUnArchiver -> extractFileIfIncluded -> extractFile) reported in the alert, so one change covers all traces. The separator is appended to the directory prefix to avoid sibling-prefix false negatives (e.g. /tmp/dest vs /tmp/dest-evil). getCanonicalPath throws IOException, which extractFile already declares. Added TarUnArchiverPathTraversalTest which builds a tar containing a "../evil.txt" entry, asserts extraction throws ArchiverException, and asserts the file is not written outside the destination directory.
output_json.risk_notes: The check uses canonical paths, which resolve symlinks; legitimate extractions (including existing symlink tests) still pass — full suite is 150 tests, 0 failures, 1 pre-existing skip. Malicious entries now throw ArchiverException instead of silently escaping, which is the intended hardening.
output_json.summary: Fixed a "Zip Slip" path traversal (CWE-022) in plexus-archiver. Archive entry names (from tar/zip) were passed unchecked to FileUtils.resolveFile in AbstractUnArchiver.extractFile, so an entry like "../evil.txt" would resolve outside the destination directory and be written/created there (mkdirs, FileOutputStream, symlink). Added a canonical-path containment check that rejects any entry resolving outside the destination directory before any filesystem write.
